rationale: This is the methcall Shootout kernel: a 9-function, ~490-byte binary whose hot loop is dominated by repeated virtual dispatch (Toggle/NthToggle activate), so runtime overhead compounds directly and size headroom is tiny. SUB and SPLIT are nearly free and give strong per-function diversity across the few functions available, so they carry the highest gain weights with minimal cost penalties. IBR and ICALL are kept as moderate options since methcall's call- and branch-heavy dispatch loop benefits from opaque indirectness, but their runtime penalties are raised because the loop is hot. FLA is allowed selectively (its flattening is the strongest control-flow hiding for the dispatch loop) but with elevated runtime/size/risk penalties so the selector only applies it where feature scores justify it. BCF is effectively discouraged (highest runtime and size penalties) because bogus control-flow bloat is disproportionate on a 256-byte main and its opaque predicates execute inside the hottest loop; IGV sits in the middle as a cheaper control-flow-scrambling alternative. CorrectnessRisk penalties are kept high across the board since the program's semantics (object-style state toggling) rely on precise call ordering and loop bounds.
